newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Rate fear hits Euro shares in New Year.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Rate fear hits Euro shares in New Year.

text.p: The fear of rising interest rates resurfaced on Thursday to chop more than one percent off Europe's key bourses in the first minutes of new year trading after Wall Street ended the old year by losing 101 points.
German shares were down 1.8 percent, French shares by 1.7 percent and London, Europe's busiest market, by around one percent in early trade, though the losses had been cut by midday.

"It's the same old story -- the fear of rising interest rates," said one London share dealer. "Given that we finished the year in a fairly strong fashion, I think we could see a rather substantial markdown and perhaps finish the day one to two percent lower."

The Dow Jones industrial average fell 101.10 points, or 1.5 percent, to 6,448.27 on Tuesday -- the biggest one-day drop on Wall Street since mid-July -- as bond yields rose to 6.64 percent from 6.54 percent on a brace of stronger-than-expected U.S. economic indicators.

The U.S. government said sales of new homes jumped a stronger-than-expected 14.2 percent in November, the steepest rise in more than 3-1/2 years. In addition, consumer confidence soared in December, jumping to a reading of 113.8 from 109.5 in November, the Conference Board said.

Traders fear that the strength of U.S. economic growth could signal a rise in inflation and lead to higher interest rates, which spell bad news for highly valued share markets as returns on other investments and holding cash on deposit rise.

Tuesday's drop put a small dent in Wall Street's rise for 1996 but coupled with its 1995 performance, the Dow has climbed around 60 percent over the last two years, a run the likes of which has been seen only twice before, in 1927-28 and 1954-55.
The market's gains in 1996 came despite widespread predictions that inflation or weak corporate earnings would rain on Wall Street's parade.
European shares chased U.S. shares higher in 1996 when British stocks chalked up a gain of 11.6 percent, Frankfurt 28 percent and French shares almost 24 percent.
While the mood was more cautious on Thursday, many traders were still on holiday and business was relatively thin.

Technical analysts in London viewed the fall as simply a correction in a bull market and pegged near-term chart support for the FTSE index at 4,065, with further support at 4,050 and major psychological support at 4,000. It stood at 4,088.6 at midday, down 29.9 points, or 0.73 percent.

Frence's CAC-40 index of leading shares opened down 0.43 percent and then fell further with the losses exaggerated in thin post-holiday trade. By midday the index was down 34.24 points, or 1.5 percent, at 2,281.49 points.

German shares fell the most but dealers said they did not expect any further strong declines amid particularly weak trading volumes and at midday the DAX index of floor trading was down 44.13 points, or 1.53 percent, at 2,844.56. They also said the dollar's slight rally was supportive for German shares.
Currency dealers said the dollar recovered some steam and was perkier against the mark and yen in Europe as the market awaited fresh U.S. economic data.
It stood at 1.5455 marks and 115.78 yen at midday compared with 1.5385 marks and 115.85 yen late on Tuesday.
Traders said U.S. jobless claims at 1330 GMT and December purchasing managers' figures were keenly awaited after Tuesday's data.
"The figures (Tuesday's) did put a spanner in the works. The figures were strong. So there will be more focus on the new data," said a trader at a leading British merchant bank.
The yen has is under pressure against the dollar on concern over the strength of Japan economy.

World oil prices began 1997 with a rally as freezing weather continued to grip much of Europe, stoking demand for winter heating oil and memories of a similar cold snap in the United States a year ago.
The February Brent crude oil futures contract on the International Petroleum Exchange (IPE) was up 47 cents a barrel at $24.28 at midday, having been up 80 cents at one point.
CURRENCIES AT 1200 GMT
The dollar stood at 1.5455 marks and 115.78 yen compared with 1.5385 marks and 115.85 yen late on Tuesday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1200 GMT
The FTSE 100 index of leading British shares was at 4,088.6, down 29.9 points.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index fell 34.24 to 2,281.49.
In Frankfurt, the 30-share DAX index slipped 44.13 points to 2,844.56.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold fixed at $367.80 compared with its late level of $369.05 in London on Tuesday.
